newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria receives fresh nuclear fuel from Russia.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria receives fresh nuclear fuel from Russia.

text.p: Bulgaria, heavily dependent on its Soviet model nuclear power plant for the coming winter, received fresh nuclear fuel from Russia on Thursday and will restart its biggest reactor in November, the plant's chairman said on Thursday.

"We are now unloading the last shipment of the rods for recharging reactor number six and plan to connect it to the national grid on November 12 as scheduled," Kiril Nikolov told Reuters by telephone.
Bulgaria, which lacks energy resources, has not enough power reserves to replace a 1,000-megawatt nuclear reactor during the winter, energy officials said.
They said the country would be able to replace only small volumes if a plant failed.
Bulgaria will be on the edge of a power crisis in January if its oldest 440-megawatt reactor cannot come on stream a month earlier, energy chiefs said.
Nikolov said Russia's Korchatov Institute, which will analyse samples of the metal of reactor number one, would speed up its tests in a bid to prepare preliminary results in mid-November.
The reactor, which was switched off in May amid international concern over its safety, will be restarted in December if it is found to be safe.
"But if results show that the metal needs thermal treatment, then the reactor will not be in operation this winter," Nikolov said.
Bulgaria, which imports more than 80 percent of its energy resources, was forced to impose power cuts between 1978 and 1993 mainly because of reactor failures.
The Kozloduy power plant provides around half the country's electricity needs. It has four VVER 440-megawatt reactors and two VVER 1,000-megawatt reactors.
